fields.label: Sales sourcing (services and intangibles)
fields.value: Receipts from services are sourced using market-based sourcing if the benefit of the service is received in New Jersey. Intangible royalties are sourced to New Jersey if used within the State, and sales of intangible assets are sourced based on net gain recognized.
fields.quote: Service Receipts and Special Industry Sourcing Rules Service receipts are sourced based on where the benefit of the service is received, which is commonly referred to as market-based sourcing.

fields.label: Special industry rules
fields.value: Special rules apply to airlines using revenue miles, combined freight transportation companies using ton-miles, and specific industries including asset management, advertising, and casinos. Regulated investment companies and investment companies may also qualify for special statutory apportionment percentages.
fields.quote: Airlines have special sourcing rules pursuant to N.J.S.A.

fields.label: Forms
fields.value: Apportionment is computed on Schedule J (Computation of Allocation Factor) for Form CBT-100 and Form CBT-100S. Combined groups use Schedule J (Computation of Group Allocation Factor) on Form CBT-100U.
fields.quote: Schedule J Computation of Allocation Factor If taxpayer does not have receipts outside New Jersey, the allocation factor will be 100% (1.000000) and there is no need to complete this schedule.

fields.label: Income/franchise tax nexus
fields.value: Corporations have CBT nexus if they have physical contacts or meet bright-line economic nexus thresholds in New Jersey. A corporation establishes bright-line economic nexus if New Jersey source receipts exceed $100,000 or it delivers 200 or more separate transactions to customers in New Jersey during the tax year.
fields.quote: or (2) The corporation has 200 or more separate transactions delivered to customers in this State during the corporation’s fiscal or calendar year.

fields.label: Sales/use tax: economic nexus
fields.value: Remote sellers must register and collect New Jersey sales tax if sales delivered into the state exceed $100,000 in gross revenue or consist of 200 or more separate transactions. This threshold is measured based on sales during the current or prior calendar year.
fields.quote: The remote seller's gross revenue from sales of tangible personal property, specified digital products, or taxable services delivered into New Jersey during the current or prior calendar year, exceeds $100,000 ;

fields.label: P.L. 86-272
fields.value: New Jersey limits P.L. 86-272 immunity strictly to solicitation of sales of tangible personal property and has adopted the Multistate Tax Commission's revised guidance treating many internet activities as exceeding protection. Protected corporations with nexus remain subject to filing obligations and the statutory minimum tax.
fields.quote: Section 381, “Public Law 86-272,” prohibits a state from imposing a net income based tax on income of a foreign corporation earned within its borders from interstate commerce, if the corporation’s only business activity within the state consists of the solicitation of orders by the corporation or its representatives of tangible personal property, the orders are sent outside the state for approval and, if approved, are filled by shipment or delivery from a point outside the state.

fields.label: Sales and use tax
fields.value: The New Jersey state sales and use tax rate is 6.625%, and local jurisdictions do not impose broad local sales taxes. However, specialized localized rates exist, including reduced rates in Urban Enterprise Zones and Salem County at 3.3125%, luxury tax adjustments in Atlantic City, and a 2% tourism tax in Cape May County.
fields.source_citation: NJ Division of Taxation - Answers to Frequently Asked Questions
fields.quote: What is the New Jersey Sales Tax rate? The State of New Jersey's Sales and Use Tax rate is (6.625%).

fields.label: Other notable business taxes
fields.value: The elective Pass-Through Business Alternative Income Tax applies to pass-through entities at rates of 5.675% up to $250,000, 6.52% from $250,001 to $1,000,000, and 10.9% over $1,000,000.

fields.label: Pass-through entity tax (PTET)
fields.value: New Jersey offers an elective Pass-Through Business Alternative Income Tax with graduated rates from 5.675% to 10.9% on distributive proceeds. The annual election and Form PTE-100 return are due by March 15 online, with a 6-month extension available using Form PTE-200-T.
fields.source_citation: NJ Division of Taxation - Pass-Through Business Alternative Income Tax (PTE/BAIT)

fields.label: Withholding and estimated payments
fields.value: Individual estimated taxes are required if expected liability exceeds withholdings and credits by more than $400, payable in four installments due April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15. Underpayment interest is avoided if payments meet the 80% current-year or 100% prior-year safe harbor.
fields.source_citation: NJ Division of Taxation - Pass-Through Business Alternative Income Tax (PTE/BAIT)
fields.quote: Form CBT-100S Members may still need NJ-1040-ES estimated tax payments for income not covered by BAIT.

fields.label: Key forms
fields.value: Key returns include Form NJ-1040 and NJ-1040NR for individuals, and Form CBT-100, CBT-100U, and CBT-100S for corporations. Pass-through entities file Form NJ-1065, Form NJ-CBT-1065, Form PTE-100, or Form NJ-1080-C.
